extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, drafters, examiners, and practitioners drafting or interpreting claim language
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for selecting and interpreting transitional phrases in patent claims (comprising, consisting of, consisting essentially of) to control claim scope and permitted additional elements. Emphasizes MPEP 2111.03 rules and reliance on the specification to determine what changes are 'material'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'consisting essentially of'
rubrics_metrics.description: “The transitional phrase ‘consisting essentially of’ limits the scope of a claim to the specified materials or steps ‘and those that do not materially affect the basic and novel characteristic(s)’ of the claimed invention.” (MPEP 2111.03)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'consisting essentially of' when you want a middle ground between fully open and fully closed claim scope. It permits additional elements only if they do not materially affect the invention's basic and novel characteristics. Example: “A cleaning composition consisting essentially of ingredients X, Y, and Z” allows minor additives that don’t significantly change cleaning properties but excludes major components that alter fundamental nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprising: open-ended transitional phrase
rubrics_metrics.description: “Comprising” is open-ended and allows for additional, unrecited elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'comprising' to keep claim scope broad and permit elements or steps beyond those recited. For claim construction and infringement analysis, it does not exclude other components. Note: For prior art searching, MPEP treats 'consisting essentially of' as equivalent to 'comprising' (see related rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consisting of: closed transitional phrase
rubrics_metrics.description: “Consisting of” is closed and excludes any element not specified in the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'consisting of' when you intend to limit the claim strictly to the recited elements or steps and to exclude any unrecited elements. Recommended wording from MPEP: 'Consisting of limits only recited elements.' Avoid 'consisting of' if you want to allow incidental or non-material additives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'consisting essentially of' requires reference to the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: When using or interpreting 'consisting essentially of,' it is important to refer to the specification to understand what constitutes a material change to the invention's basic and novel characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specification should be consulted and used to identify the invention's basic and novel characteristics; what is 'material' is determined in light of that disclosure. Draft the specification to explicitly define those characteristics if you intend to rely on 'consisting essentially of' to permit some but not all additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification must define basic and novel characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification should define the basic and novel characteristics of the invention (MPEP 2111.03).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To make 'consisting essentially of' meaningful, identify and describe in the specification which characteristics are basic and novel so that determinations about material effect can be made. Failure to do so can create ambiguity in claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consisting essentially of considered equivalent to comprising for prior art search
rubrics_metrics.description: Per MPEP 2111.03: 'Consisting Essentially Of Is Equivalent To Comprising For Prior Art Search.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When conducting prior art/novelty searches, treat 'consisting essentially of' as if it were open-ended ('comprising') so that prior art that includes additional components may still be relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method claim steps must not materially affect novel characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP 2111.03 indicates that method claim steps must not materially affect the basic and novel characteristics when 'consisting essentially of' is used for steps or materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drafting method claims using 'consisting essentially of' (or interpreting them), evaluate whether additional steps would materially alter the invention's novel characteristics; if so, those steps are excluded. Drafting should make clear which characteristics are protected from material alteration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of claim is defined by choice of transitional phrase
rubrics_metrics.description: Transitional phrases (e.g., comprising, consisting essentially of, consisting of) define the scope of a claim (MPEP 2111.03).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the transitional phrase deliberately to achieve the intended breadth or narrowness of the claim. Be aware that each phrase carries different presumptive effects on inclusion/exclusion of unrecited elements and can affect infringement, validity, and prior art considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'consisting essentially of' for 'middle ground' composition claim format
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP guidance: 'Consisting essentially of' is the transitional phrase for a middle ground composition claim format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ this phrase when you want to allow minor/non-material additives in a composition claim while excluding changes that would alter fundamental properties. Ensure specification support for what is non-material versus material to the invention's basic and novel characteristics.
